title: AI’s Giant Money Loop Is Feeling Very 2008
description_html:
The AI infrastructure boom is funded by a complex web of investments, as tech companies pour money into one another and foreign investors funnel still more cash into the industry. That flow of foreign money is also creating global imbalances — and flashbacks to the run-up to the 2008 financial crisis.

On today’s Big Take podcast, Bloomberg’s Shawn Donnan and Bloomberg Economics’ Tom Orlik join David Gura on the AI industry’s global money machine: how it works and what risks it could pose to the global economy if the AI trade doesn’t deliver fast enough. 

Read more:

  • AI’s Giant Money Loop Is Drawing Foreign Cash Like 2008
  • National Bureau of Economic Research: Financing the AI Buildout

segments.text: So it's notoriously hard to call bubbles, right? And clearly there is real potential. with this technology and if you look at the revenue run rate for anthropic for example well it's already a technology which is delivering on that promise right that said valuations do look very very elevated a couple of things which caught my eye recently first planned ipo of an australian data center company was pulled in the last few days um apparently because investors thought the valuation was too rich.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: OpenAI, also generating quite a lot of revenue, but the latest news suggesting the run rate for 2026 isn't quite as high as investors thought it would be. So is it a bubble? Is the bubble about to burst? Don't know the answer, but the more there is that trickle of bad news, the more chance there is that a moment of reckoning arrives.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We should also be clear that, you know, just as we have seen big capital investment episodes in US history that have turned out to be incredibly good for the economy in the longer term, they often have been associated with a downturn. So the 1890s, the railway investment boom, is, goes gangbusters, and then it turns and the economy goes into a recession afterwards. But, you know, we would all argue that railways were good for the U.S. economy in the longer run.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The dot-com boom in the 2000s, you know, it came after a huge build-out in terms of fiber optic networks and so on that, again, have been good for the long run for the U.S. economy, but some of the valuations got ahead of things. You had a recession that came along there. There was an amazing paper that came out of Brookings and the National Bureau of Economic Research just in the last few weeks out of a Columbia Business School professor who made the point that between 2025 and 2032, the total amount of capital that will go into the AI build-out will be around $9 trillion, or about 3.2% of GDP a year.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And that is bigger than the railway investment boom of the 1890s. That makes it the biggest capital investment boom that we've seen in US history. So just putting that in context, history also tells us that these things may be good in the long run, but there's bumps along the way.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: This is The Big Take from Bloomberg News. I'm David Gurra. To get more from The Big Take and unlimited access to all of Bloomberg.com, subscribe today at Bloomberg.com slash podcast offer.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Thanks for listening. We'll be back tomorrow.

study.one_liner_ko: AI 칩 수요가 아시아에 쌓인 달러 저축을 다시 미국 AI 기업으로 되돌려 보내는 거대한 자금 순환이 2008년 위기 직전의 글로벌 불균형을 연상시킨다는 분석이다.
summary_ko: 미국의 AI 칩 수요가 한국·대만으로 달러를 보내고, 그 저축이 다시 미국 주식·채권 시장과 AI 기업으로 흘러든다. 글로벌 불균형이 150년 만의 최고 수준 근처까지 올라왔다.
2000년대 초에는 신중한 중앙은행이 가장 안전한 자산인 미 국채를 샀다. 지금은 수익을 좇는 민간 투자자가 AI 하이퍼스케일러에 돈을 대고 있어 훨씬 민첩하고 불안정하다.
AI 자산이 자금을 빨아들이면서 미 국채 수요가 줄고 있다. 10년물 금리는 5%를 넘었고 연간 이자 비용은 1조 달러가 넘는다. 2000년대 초에는 외국 저축이 금리를 낮췄지만 지금은 반대다.
AI 기대가 꺾이면 AI 기업과 투자자가 타격을 입고, 칩을 수출하고 그 이익을 다시 투자한 한국·대만 같은 '테크노 국가'는 이중으로 타격을 받는다. 자원 의존국의 '네덜란드병'과 비슷하다는 경고도 나온다.
미국 GDP 성장의 최대 1%포인트가 AI 투자에서 나온다는 추정이 있어, 붕괴하면 미국 경기 둔화가 세계로 퍼진다.
버블 여부는 터진 뒤에야 알 수 있다. 호주 데이터센터 IPO 철회, OpenAI 매출 전망 하향 같은 악재가 쌓이고 있다. 다만 철도·닷컴 때처럼 장기적으로는 경제에 득이 되어도 중간에 침체가 올 수 있다.
study.summary_en: So this episode is about a giant money loop behind the AI boom. The US buys huge numbers of AI chips from Korea and Taiwan, those economies pile up dollars, and the money flows right back into US markets and the very AI companies buying the chips. Global imbalances are near their highest in 150 years. The big difference from 2008 is that nimble private investors, not cautious central banks, are moving the money, and they're funding AI hyperscalers instead of Treasuries. If the payoff doesn't come fast enough, the tech-heavy Asian economies get hit twice. History says big build-outs can be great long term, but there are bumps along the way.

expressions.quote: This is kind of the thing that keeps you up at night
expressions.meaning_ko: 밤잠을 설치게 할 만큼 걱정거리가 되다
expressions.nuance_ko: 'What keeps you up at night?'은 인터뷰나 패널에서 가장 큰 리스크를 물을 때 자주 쓴다. 실제 불면이 아니라 핵심 우려를 뜻한다. 격식 없이 두루 쓸 수 있다.
examples: Honestly, the thing that keeps me up at night is losing our two best engineers.
So what keeps you up at night when you think about the election?
Rising rent is what keeps most of my friends up at night.

similar.example: The layoffs have been weighing on my mind all week.
Inflation is a major worry for most households right now.

expressions.quote: if it doesn't live up to its promise
expressions.nuance_ko: live up to the hype / expectations / billing도 같이 쓴다. 주로 부정문이나 if절로 기대 대비 실망을 말할 때 쓴다. 비즈니스와 일상 모두 자연스럽다.
examples: The new CRM never really lived up to its promise.
The restaurant didn't live up to the hype, to be honest.
If the merger lives up to its promise, we'll all benefit.

similar.example: The movie didn't quite live up to the hype.
They need to deliver on what they promised the board.

expressions.quote: it will ripple out through the global economy
expressions.nuance_ko: 한 충격이 잔물결처럼 시스템 전체로 퍼지는 이미지다. 경제·정치·조직 변화에 모두 쓴다. 'ripple effect', 'send ripples through'도 자주 쓴다.
examples: A port strike in one city can ripple out through the whole supply chain.
The CEO's resignation rippled out through the entire company.
That one viral post rippled out through the whole community.

similar.example: The announcement sent shockwaves through the industry.
The delay will have a knock-on effect on every other team.

expressions.quote: you kind of perk up, take notice
expressions.nuance_ko: perk up은 갑자기 관심이 생겨 기운을 차리는 느낌이다. 'sit up and take notice'도 같은 계열이다. 어떤 신호에 반응이 즉각적일 때 쓴다.
examples: When I heard the word 'acquisition', I perked up right away.
Investors tend to perk up when the Fed changes its tone.
She perked up the moment someone mentioned a free trip.

similar.example: That growth number made everyone sit up and take notice.
I pricked up my ears when they mentioned my team.

expressions.quote: I would echo the points that Sean made
expressions.nuance_ko: 패널에서 앞사람 의견에 동의를 표시한 뒤 'and I'd add…'로 자기 논점을 얹는 전형적 시작 패턴이다. 'I'd echo that'만으로도 쓴다. 격식 있고 세련된 느낌이다.
examples: I'd echo what Maria said about the timeline, and add one concern on budget.
I'd echo that. We saw the same thing in our own numbers.
Let me echo Jason's point and push it a bit further.

similar.example: I second that. The onboarding process needs a rewrite.
Let me build on that for a second.

expressions.nuance_ko: 'Good intentions aren't a blank check'처럼 좋은 명분이 모든 걸 정당화하지 못한다는 뜻으로 쓴다. 예산이나 권한을 제한 없이 주는 상황에도 쓴다. 비판적 논조에서 효과적이다.
examples: A big win in the polls isn't a blank check to do whatever you want.
We can't give the vendor a blank check just because they're experienced.
My boss said the budget isn't a blank check, so I have to justify each item.

similar.example: They gave her carte blanche to redesign the whole office.
He had free rein over the project.

expressions.quote: So if all of this turns south, they face a double blow.
expressions.nuance_ko: go south와 같은 뜻으로, 시장·협상·계획이 틀어질 때 쓴다. 구어체지만 뉴스·회의에서도 통한다. 'if things turn south'가 가장 흔한 형태다.
examples: If the negotiation turns south, we need a fallback plan.
The whole trip turned south when our flight got cancelled.
Markets turned south right after the earnings call.

similar.example: The launch went sideways because of a bug.

similar.expression: take a turn for the worse
similar.example: Things took a turn for the worse in the second half.

expressions.meaning_ko: 결국 현실을 직시하고 대가를 치르는 순간
expressions.nuance_ko: 오래 미뤄온 문제나 과열된 낙관이 현실과 부딪히는 때를 말한다. 'a day of reckoning'도 같은 말이다. 진지하고 다소 극적인 어조다.

expressions.meaning_ko: 그 부분을 이어서 말해 달라 / 이어받다
expressions.nuance_ko: 사회자·회의 진행자가 상대의 논점을 이어받아 더 풀어 달라고 요청할 때 쓰는 표현이다. 직접 말할 때는 'Let me pick up on that'으로 쓴다. 대화 흐름을 부드럽게 넘기는 도구다.
examples: Priya, can you pick up on that point about hiring?
Let me pick up on something Tom mentioned earlier.
I'd like to pick up on your comment about pricing.

similar.example: Could you expand on that a little?
I'll follow up on that after the meeting.

expressions.quote: some of the valuations got ahead of things
expressions.nuance_ko: 여기서는 가격이 펀더멘털을 앞질렀다는 완곡한 표현이다. 'get ahead of oneself'(너무 앞서 나가다)와 함께 알아두면 좋다. 버블을 직접 단정하지 않고 돌려 말할 때 유용하다.
examples: I think we got ahead of ourselves announcing the date before the contract was signed.
Prices got ahead of things last year, so the correction isn't surprising.
Let's not get ahead of things. We haven't even seen the data yet.

similar.example: I'm getting ahead of myself, but I already picked the venue.
The rally ran ahead of fundamentals.

expressions.quote: that said valuations do look very very elevated
expressions.meaning_ko: 그렇긴 하지만 (앞 내용을 인정한 뒤 반론)
expressions.nuance_ko: 앞 문장을 인정한 뒤 균형을 잡는 'however'의 구어형이다. 한 번 양보한 뒤 진짜 하고 싶은 말을 꺼낼 때 쓴다. 'Having said that'도 같은 용법이다.
examples: The product is great. That said, the pricing is going to be a hard sell.
I love the city. That said, I wouldn't want to live there year-round.
He's a strong candidate. That said, I'd want to check a few references.

similar.example: Having said that, we shouldn't ignore the risks.
Even so, it's worth a try.

expressions.expression: on the other side of the ledger
expressions.quote: on the other side of the ledger
expressions.nuance_ko: 장부의 대변·차변 이미지에서 나온 말로, 이익 대 손실처럼 대비되는 요소를 이어갈 때 쓴다. 논점을 '한편으로는 / 다른 한편으로는' 구조로 정리하기 좋다. 'on the plus side'보다 분석적인 느낌이다.
examples: We have a strong brand. On the other side of the ledger, our costs are rising fast.
Remote work saves commute time. On the other side of the ledger, you lose casual chats.
The salary is great, but on the other side of the ledger, the hours are brutal.

similar.example: On the flip side, it's way cheaper.
The downside is you have to commit for two years.

warmup.q: When you hear that something is a 'bubble', what's your first reaction? Do you get worried or curious?
warmup.hint_ko: 버블이라는 말에 대한 개인적 반응, 과거 경험(부동산·코인 등)을 예로 들어 말해 본다.

warmup.q: What keeps you up at night when you think about the global economy right now?
warmup.hint_ko: 가장 큰 거시 리스크 하나를 고르고 이유를 한두 가지로 설명한다.

opinion.q: The episode says the actors have changed since 2008: nimble private investors instead of cautious central banks. Does that make the system more fragile or more resilient?
opinion.hint_ko: 민첩성의 장점(빠른 자금 재배분)과 단점(빠른 이탈, 쏠림)을 비교하고 결론을 낸다.

opinion.q: Past booms like railways and fiber optics were good in the long run but painful along the way. How should investors and policymakers think about that trade-off?
opinion.hint_ko: 장기 이익 vs 단기 침체, 개인 투자자와 정책 당국의 관점 차이를 들어 말한다.

debate.q: Is the AI investment boom a genuine productivity story or mostly a financial bubble?
debate.for: Genuine productivity: revenue run rates are real, adoption is fast, and past build-outs like railways and fiber paid off in the long run.
debate.against: Bubble: valuations look elevated, IPOs are being pulled, circular financing inflates demand, and the capital spending is bigger than any boom before it.

debate.q: Should countries like South Korea and Taiwan deliberately diversify away from chips even if it means giving up short-term gains?
debate.for: Yes: over-concentration creates Dutch-disease-style risk, and a downturn would hit them twice, through exports and through their investments.
debate.against: No: their comparative advantage is in chips, diversifying means giving up profits and scale, and the market will correct concentration on its own.

roleplay.scenario: You are on a panel about whether the AI boom is a risk to the global economy. The moderator asks you to respond to a fellow panelist who is very bullish and dismisses comparisons to 2008.
roleplay.your_role: A cautious economist who acknowledges the upside but explains the risks
roleplay.partner_role: A bullish tech investor who thinks the 2008 comparison is overblown (also acts as moderator)
goals: Open by echoing a point your partner made, then use 'That said' to introduce your concerns

useful_phrases.phrase: I'd echo that, and I'd add one thing.

shadowing.reason_ko: 'on one side... on the other side' 대비 구조와 'the imbalances are back, but the actors have changed'처럼 핵심을 한 문장으로 요약하는 리듬을 익히기 좋다.
'Don't know the answer, but the more... the more...' 비교 구문과 불확실성을 솔직하게 말하는 톤을 연습하기 좋다.
수치를 맥락화하고 'history also tells us... bumps along the way'로 결론을 맺는 패널 마무리 화법의 좋은 모델이다.

difficulty.note_ko: 거시경제 용어(global imbalances, current account surplus, Dutch disease)가 많고 말 속도가 빠르다. 구어체 담화 표지와 관용구는 비교적 평이해서 그대로 재사용하기 좋다.

translations_sent.50-50: 하지만 어느 순간 시장이 이렇게 말한다면 어떨까요?

translations_sent.88-88: 전 세계의 자본을 그대로 흡수하고 있으니까요.

translations_sent.92-92: 그러면 미국이 매년 내는 이자 비용이 1조 달러가 넘는다는 뜻이고, 그 돈은 교육이나 국방, 인프라에 쓸 수도 있는 돈입니다.

translations_sent.130-130: 사람들이 말하는 또 다른 큰 요인은, 지금 미국 성장의 상당 부분이 이 AI 투자 붐에서 나오고 있다는 겁니다.

translations_sent.150-150: 하지만 철도가 장기적으로 미국 경제에 좋았다는 데는 우리 모두 동의할 겁니다.
translations_sent.151-151: 2000년대의 닷컴 붐도 광케이블망 같은 대규모 구축 뒤에 왔는데, 그것 역시 장기적으로는 미국 경제에 좋았지만 일부 밸류에이션이 앞서 나갔죠.
translations_sent.153-153: 불과 몇 주 전에 브루킹스와 전미경제연구소에서 컬럼비아 경영대학원 교수가 쓴 놀라운 논문이 나왔는데, 2025년부터 2032년까지 AI 구축에 들어갈 자본 총액이 약 9조 달러, 즉 매년 GDP의 약 3.2%에 이를 거라고 했습니다.
translations_sent.154-154: 이건 1890년대 철도 투자 붐보다 더 큰 규모입니다.
translations_sent.155-155: 미국 역사상 가장 큰 자본 투자 붐이 되는 셈이죠.
translations_sent.156-156: 맥락을 위해 말씀드리자면, 역사는 이런 일들이 장기적으로는 좋을 수 있지만 그 과정에 굴곡이 있다고도 알려줍니다.
